spec.description: Write one record into a collection of the account's repository. A post is exactly this, with `collection: "app.bsky.feed.post"` and a record carrying `text` and `createdAt`.

repo.description: The repository to write in: a DID or a handle. The session's own `did` in every ordinary use.

collection.description: NSID of the collection, such as `app.bsky.feed.post` for a post. Any NSID is accepted -- a PDS stores records in collections nothing renders, which is how this client's examples are recorded without publishing anything.

record.description: The record itself. Its shape is the collection's own lexicon, which this spec does not model: a `app.bsky.feed.post` wants `$type`, `text` and `createdAt`, and a custom collection wants whatever its author says. Declared as a free-form object rather than a union of every lexicon, because the set is open by design.

additionalProperties.description: One field of the record, as its lexicon defines it.

rkey.description: Record key. Generated by the server when omitted, which is the normal case.

validate.description: Ask the server to check the record against its lexicon. `validate` is the name every generated method already reserves for its own response-validation override, so the backend renames this one: the Python method takes it as `validate_`. The wire name is unchanged.

uri.description: AT URI of the new record (`at://<did>/<collection>/<rkey>`).

cid.description: CID of this version of it.

validationStatus.description: `valid` when the server checked the record against its lexicon, `unknown` when it has no lexicon to check against -- which is what a custom collection gets.

notes: `validate` collides with the reserved parameter name every generated method carries for response validation (authoring rule 10 and standard S8), so the backend renames it. It renames it to `validate_`, not to anything descriptive -- an earlier version of this note claimed `validate_record`, which was what I expected rather than what it does. Checked against the generated signature.
